chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isa, all from Yunus, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, from Zurarah, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the grandfather (in inheritance), so he said: 'No one has given a ruling on it except by his own opinion, except for the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).' I said: 'May God perfect you, so what did the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) say about it?' He said: 'When it is tomorrow, wait for me until I read it to you from the book of Ali (peace be upon him).' I said: 'May God perfect you, narrate to me, for your narration is more beloved to me than you reading it to me from a book.' So he said to me for the third time: 'Listen to what I say to you: when it is tomorrow, wait for me until I read it to you from a book.'

So I went to him the next day after Dhuhr prayer, and it was my time when I would be alone with him between Dhuhr and Asr. I disliked asking him unless I was alone, fearing that he might give a ruling in the presence of others due to precaution (taqiyyah). So when I entered upon him, he turned to his son Ja'far and said: 'Read to Zurarah the sheet of inheritances.' Then he rose to sleep, so I and Ja'far remained in the house. He rose and brought out to me a sheet like the thigh of a camel, and said: 'I will not read it to you until you make it so that you do not narrate to anyone what you read in it ever, until I give you permission.' And he did not say 'until my father gives you permission.' I said: 'May God perfect you, why do you restrict me, and your father did not command you with that?' He said: 'You are not looking at it except according to what I said to you.'

So I said: 'That is for you.' I was a man knowledgeable about inheritances and bequests, perceptive of them, and calculating them. I spent time seeking something said about inheritances and bequests that I did not know, so I could not find it. So when he threw to me the edge of the sheet, it was a thick book, known to be from the books of the early ones. I looked, and it was contrary to what was in the hands of people, of the solid and the command of the well-known, which had no difference, and most of it was like that. So I read it until I reached its end with the foulness of the soul, little caution, and diseases of opinion, and I said while I was reading it: 'It is false,' until I reached its end. Then I rolled it up and handed it to him.

So when morning came, I met Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and he said to me: 'Did you read the sheet of inheritances?' I said: 'Yes.' He said: 'How did you see what you read?' I said: 'False, it is nothing, it is contrary to what people are upon.' He said: 'By God, O Zurarah, what you saw is the truth, what you saw is the dictation of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and the handwriting of Ali (peace be upon him) with his own hand.'

Then Satan came to me and whispered in my chest, saying: 'And what does he know that it is the dictation of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and the handwriting of Ali (peace be upon him) with his own hand?' He said to me before I spoke: 'O Zurarah, do not doubt.' And the beloved of Satan, by God, is that you doubted. And how would I not know that it is the dictation of the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) and the handwriting of Ali (peace be upon him) with his own hand, when my father had narrated to me from my grandfather that the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) had told him that.
I said: 'No, how? May God make me your ransom.' And I regretted what had escaped me from the book, and if I had read it while I knew it, I would have hoped that not a letter of it would escape me.

Umar ibn Udhaynah said: I said to Zurarah: 'Indeed, some people narrated to me from him and from his father about matters in inheritances, so I will present them to you. Whatever of them is false, say: This is false, and whatever of them is true, say: This is true, and do not narrate it and be silent.' So I narrated to him what Muhammad ibn Muslim had narrated to me from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the daughter and the father, the daughter and the mother, and the two parents. He said: 'By God, it is the truth.'

key_terms.إِمْلاءُ رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: Dictation of the Messenger of God
key_terms.صَحِيفَة: Sheet or large page of writing

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Zurarah and the sheet of inheritance rulings from Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the concept of *al-Sahifa al-Faraid* (the Sheet of Inheritance), a foundational text attributed to Imam Ali, which contains rulings that sometimes diverge from the consensus of the early jurists. Imam al-Baqir confirms its authenticity as the Prophet's dictation and Ali's handwriting, using Zurarah’s initial skepticism to illustrate the need for deep scholarly verification (*tahqiq*) when reconciling transmitted texts with prevailing legal opinions. It underscores the Shia principle that authoritative inherited texts may preserve distinct legal nuances not immediately apparent to the general scholarly community.
